name: Geometry of Straight Lines
what_is_it: This topic studies angles formed when straight lines meet or cross, including angles on a straight line, around a point, vertically opposite angles, and angles formed by a transversal crossing parallel lines.
why_it_matters: Angle relationships are the building blocks for proving properties of shapes, reading construction/engineering plans, and every later geometry topic including Pythagoras and trigonometry.
key_vocabulary: Angle — the amount of turn between two rays meeting at a point (vertex)
Straight angle — an angle of exactly 180°
Vertically opposite angles — the equal angles formed on opposite sides when two lines cross
Transversal — a line that crosses two or more other lines
Parallel lines — lines that never meet and stay the same distance apart
Corresponding, alternate, and co-interior angles — special angle pairs formed when a transversal crosses parallel lines
core_concept: Certain angle pairs always add up to a fixed total (180° or 360°), or are always exactly equal, based only on the geometric arrangement of the lines — no measuring required, just applying the rule.
rules: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Angles around a point add up to 360°.
When a transversal crosses PARALLEL lines: corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, co-interior (allied) angles add up to 180°.
formulae: Angles around a point: a + b + c + ... = 360°
Co-interior angles: a + b = 180° (only if lines are parallel)
step_by_step_method: STEP 1: Identify what type of angle pair you are looking at (straight line, point, vertically opposite, or transversal pair).
STEP 2: State the geometric rule that applies (e.g. 'angles on a straight line').
STEP 3: Write an equation using the rule.
STEP 4: Solve for the unknown angle.
STEP 5: Always give a geometric REASON next to your answer (this is required in CAPS exams).

worked_example_1.question: Two angles on a straight line are x and 65°. Find x.
worked_example_1.solution:
x + 65° = 180°  (angles on a straight line)
x = 180° − 65° = 115°

worked_example_2.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 70°. Find the other.
worked_example_2.solution:
Co-interior angles add up to 180° (lines are parallel)
Other angle = 180° − 70° = 110°

fast_method: Learn to instantly recognise the angle 'shape' pattern: a Z-shape means alternate angles (equal), an F-shape means corresponding angles (equal), a C/U-shape means co-interior angles (sum to 180°).
why_fast_method_works: These letter shapes are visual shortcuts for the geometric relationship — once you can spot the shape in a diagram you instantly know the rule, without re-deriving it.
common_mistakes: Assuming angles are equal or supplementary without first checking the lines are actually parallel.
Mixing up alternate angles (Z, equal) with co-interior angles (C, sum to 180°).
Forgetting to state the geometric reason in the final answer.
Misreading which angles in a diagram are vertically opposite versus adjacent.
memory_trick: "Z is for eZual (alternate, equal). F is For the same corresponding position. C is for Co-interior, they Combine to 180°."
visual_explanation: Learnly's geometry canvas draws two parallel lines crossed by a transversal, labelling all eight angles so the learner can visually identify each pair type.
guided_example:
Find x if x and 3x are angles on a straight line.
1) x + 3x = 180°
2) 4x = 180°
3) x = 45°
(so the two angles are 45° and 135°)
practice_questions: Angles on a straight line: x and 110°. Find x.
Angles around a point: 90°, 120°, and y. Find y.
challenge_question: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle is (2x + 10)° and its co-interior angle is (3x − 30)°. Find x and both angles.
quick_test: Angles on a straight line sum to? (180°)
Angles around a point sum to? (360°)
mastery_check: Mastered when a student can identify the correct angle relationship from a diagram, set up the equation, solve it, and state the correct geometric reason without prompting.
